title: Module 5: Message Queues 📬
content: Understanding Point-to-Point Messaging in AMPS
Competitive Consumption & Worker Farms
Ensuring 'Once-and-Only-Once' Processing
speakerNotes: Welcome to Module 5. Today we shift from Pub/Sub to Message Queues. In Pub/Sub, everyone gets a copy. In Queues, only ONE person gets the message.

title: Pub/Sub vs. Queues 🎯
content: **Pub/Sub**: One-to-Many 📢. Every subscriber gets every message.
**Queues**: One-to-One 👤. One message = One consumer.
**The Goal**: Distribute work across multiple workers without duplication.
AMPS uses the same `subscribe` command but with queue semantics.
speakerNotes: Think of Pub/Sub like a radio broadcast. Think of Queues like a task list where one worker grabs one task.

title: Competitive Consumption 🏎️
content: Multiple consumers subscribe to the same queue topic.
AMPS acts as the 'Load Balancer'.
Messages are distributed based on consumer capacity and availability.
Prevents any single worker from being overwhelmed while others are idle.

content: Workers compete for messages in the queue.

title: Built on Transaction Logs 📚
content: AMPS Queues are not 'separate' storage.
They are a view over the **Transaction Log**.
Advantage: Queues are persistent across restarts.
Advantage: You can replicate queues for High Availability.
speakerNotes: Because queues are based on the transaction log, they inherit all the reliability and speed of the AMPS engine.

title: The max_backlog Pattern 🚧
content: **max_backlog**: The number of unacknowledged messages a consumer can hold.
Workers on slow hardware set low backlog (e.g., 2).
Workers on powerful hardware set high backlog (e.g., 50).
AMPS uses this to balance delivery proportionally.

title: Delivery Strategies ⚖️
content: **Round Robin**: Strict rotation among consumers.
**Proportional**: Based on `max_backlog` ratios.
**Least Loaded**: Prioritizes workers with the most free 'slots'.
Configurable via the `<Strategy>` tag in the SOW configuration.

title: Lease Period & Acknowledgement ✅
content: When a message is delivered, it is 'Leased' to the consumer.
The consumer must process it and send a `sow_delete` (Ack).
If the **Lease Period** (e.g., 10m) expires without an Ack, AMPS takes it back.
The message is then redelivered to the next available consumer.
speakerNotes: The sow_delete command is how AMPS knows you're done. If you crash, the lease expires and AMPS gives the task to someone else.

title: Handling Failure: Redelivery 🔄
content: **At-Least-Once**: Default semantics ensuring no message is lost.
**MaxDeliveries**: How many times to try before giving up?
Prevents 'Poison Messages' from crashing workers repeatedly.
Dead Letter Queues: Where failed messages go for human review.

title: Queue Configuration ⚙️
content: Queues are defined in the `<SOW>` section.
Example:

<Queue>
  <Name>WorkToDo</Name>
  <UnderlyingTopic>Work</UnderlyingTopic>
  <LeasePeriod>10m</LeasePeriod>
  <MaxDeliveries>5</MaxDeliveries>
</Queue>

title: Distributed Queues: Replicated Scale 🌐
content: Queues work across multiple AMPS instances.
Replication ensures both instances know who 'owns' the message.
Prevents duplicate processing even if the primary server fails.
Enables geographically distributed worker farms.

title: Message Expiration ⏳
content: Not every message is valid forever.
**Expiration**: Set a TTL (e.g., 1h) for queue items.
Expired messages are automatically removed from the active queue.
Useful for time-sensitive tasks like quote updates or ephemeral signals.

title: Use Case: Worker Farms 🛠️
content: Scenario: CPU-heavy risk calculations.
Solution: 50 workers subscribed to 'Risk_Queue'.
Benefit: Automatic load balancing, automatic recovery on crash.
Result: Massive horizontal scalability with zero custom logic.

title: Summary: Mastering Queues 📝
content: ✅ Queues provide Point-to-Point delivery.
✅ Built on Transaction Logs for durability.
✅ Competitive Consumption for fair load balancing.
✅ Distributed Queues for global scale.
